title: Building sentences with som
goal: Use som to add clear relative clauses about people and things.

objectives.statement: Use som to add clear relative clauses about people and things.

sections.title: A first day at the community workshop

spans.value: Lea has volunteered to help at a community repair workshop. She knows where she is supposed to work, but she does not know the people or equipment yet. Amir shows her around.
Hvem er mannen som snakker med Nora?

blocks.translation: Who is the man who is talking to Nora?

spans.value: Det er Erik. Det er han som har nøkkelen til verktøyrommet.

blocks.translation: That’s Erik. He’s the one who has the key to the tool room.

spans.value: Jeg trenger en lader som passer til denne PC-en.

blocks.translation: I need a charger that fits this computer.

spans.value: Det ligger en lader i skapet som står ved vinduet.

blocks.translation: There is a charger in the cupboard that stands by the window.

spans.value: Er det skapet som ikke kan låses?

blocks.translation: Is it the cupboard that can’t be locked?

spans.value: Ja. Og kvinnen som du møtte ved inngangen, kan hjelpe deg. Hun heter Sara.

blocks.translation: Yes. And the woman whom you met at the entrance can help you. Her name is Sara.

spans.value: Flott. Jeg har også med en lampe som jeg vil reparere.

blocks.translation: Great. I’ve also brought a lamp that I want to repair.

spans.value: Lea needs to identify particular people and things. Instead of producing many short sentences, she uses som to connect each person or thing to useful extra information:

no.value: mannen som snakker med Nora

en.value: the man who is talking to Nora

no.value: en lader som passer til denne PC-en

en.value: a charger that fits this computer

no.value: kvinnen som du møtte

en.value: the woman whom you met

no.value: en lampe som jeg vil reparere

en.value: a lamp that I want to repair

spans.value: The information after som tells Amir exactly which man, charger, woman, or lamp Lea means.

sections.title: Adding information with a relative clause

spans.value: A clause beginning with som can describe a person or thing already mentioned. This is called a
relative clause (relativsetning)
Compare two separate sentences with one connected sentence:

no.value: Jeg kjenner en mann. Mannen reparerer sykler.

en.value: I know a man. The man repairs bicycles.

no.value: Jeg kjenner en mann som reparerer sykler.

en.value: I know a man who repairs bicycles.

spans.value: The noun en mann introduces the person. The relative clause som reparerer sykler adds information about him.
The same structure works for things:

no.value: Vi har et skap. Skapet står ved vinduet.

en.value: We have a cupboard. The cupboard stands by the window.

no.value: Vi har et skap som står ved vinduet.

en.value: We have a cupboard that stands by the window.

spans.value: In English, the connecting word may be who, that, or which. Norwegian normally uses som for both people and things:

no.value: en frivillig som hjelper nye deltakere

en.value: a volunteer who helps new participants

no.value: et verktøy som er lett å bruke

en.value: a tool that is easy to use

no.value: maskiner som lager mye støy

en.value: machines that make a lot of noise

spans.value: Som does not change according to gender or number. It remains som after en-words, et-words, and plural nouns.

no.value: en lampe som virker

en.value: a lamp that works

no.value: et lys som virker

en.value: a light that works

no.value: to lamper som virker

en.value: two lamps that work

spans.value: A compact rule is:

statement.value: In the simple patterns practiced here, keep the som-clause next to the noun phrase being described, then complete the added clause.

sections.title: When the person or thing performs the action

spans.value: In several lines from the dialogue, the noun before som performs the action in the relative clause:

no.value: mannen som snakker med Nora

en.value: the man who is talking to Nora

spans.value: The man is talking, so the pattern is:
noun + som + verb

no.value: Det er Sara som leder kurset.

en.value: Sara is the one who leads the course.

no.value: Jeg trenger en kollega som kan hjelpe meg.

en.value: I need a colleague who can help me.

no.value: Vi bruker et program som fungerer på gamle PC-er.

en.value: We use a program that works on old computers.

no.value: Hun har sko som tåler mye regn.

en.value: She has shoes that withstand a lot of rain.

spans.value: The finite verb expresses the intended tense or modal form but does not change for person or number, and som remains unchanged.

no.value: Jeg kjenner en student som bor i Bergen.

en.value: I know a student who lives in Bergen.

no.value: Jeg kjenner to studenter som bor i Bergen.

en.value: I know two students who live in Bergen.

spans.value: Do not add another subject pronoun when som already represents the person or thing performing the action.
Incorrect for the intended meaning:

no.value: Jeg kjenner en mann som han jobber her.

en.value: 'Incorrect: I know a man who he works here.'

spans.value: Correct:

no.value: Jeg kjenner en mann som jobber her.

en.value: I know a man who works here.

spans.value: The word han is unnecessary because som already connects en mann to jobber.

sections.title: When another person performs the action

spans.value: Now look at Sara in the dialogue:

no.value: kvinnen som du møtte ved inngangen

en.value: the woman whom you met at the entrance

spans.value: Here, the woman does not perform the action. Du performs the action: you met the woman. Norwegian still uses som, but the acting subject comes after it:
noun + som + subject + verb

no.value: Jeg kjenner kvinnen som du møtte.

en.value: I know the woman whom you met.

no.value: Dette er boka som Amir anbefalte.

en.value: This is the book that Amir recommended.

no.value: Hvor er verktøyet som vi brukte i går?

en.value: Where is the tool that we used yesterday?

no.value: Hun fant lampen som jeg ville reparere.

en.value: She found the lamp that I wanted to repair.

spans.value: Compare the two patterns carefully:

no.value: Jeg kjenner mannen som reparerer lampen.

en.value: I know the man who repairs the lamp.

spans.value: The man repairs the lamp.

no.value: Jeg kjenner mannen som Lea møtte.

en.value: I know the man whom Lea met.

spans.value: Lea met the man.
The words immediately after som help show who performs the action:

no.value: som reparerer

en.value: the described person performs the action

no.value: som Lea møtte

en.value: Lea performs the action

spans.value: Do not repeat the described noun with a pronoun at the end of the clause.
Incorrect:

no.value: Dette er boka som jeg kjøpte den.

en.value: 'Incorrect: This is the book that I bought it.'

spans.value: Correct:

no.value: Dette er boka som jeg kjøpte.

en.value: This is the book that I bought.

spans.value: Boka is already connected to kjøpte by som. Adding den repeats the same object.

sections.title: Keeping the added information close to the noun phrase

spans.value: In the simple patterns practiced here, keep a som-clause next to the noun phrase it describes. This helps the listener understand the intended connection.

no.value: Jeg snakket med læreren som underviser i norsk.

en.value: I spoke with the teacher who teaches Norwegian.

no.value: Vi fant nøkkelen som lå under stolen.

en.value: We found the key that was under the chair.

spans.value: The relative clause describes læreren.
The relative clause describes nøkkelen.
Placement can affect meaning when a sentence contains several nouns. Return to Amir’s instruction:

no.value: Det ligger en lader i skapet som står ved vinduet.

en.value: There is a charger in the cupboard that stands by the window.

spans.value: In this simple sentence, the som-clause is placed next to the noun phrase ending in skapet, and the context makes the cupboard the intended referent. The cupboard stands by the window.
If Amir wants to describe the charger instead, he should organize this simple sentence so that the som-clause is clearly connected to the noun phrase for the charger:

no.value: Laderen som passer til denne PC-en, ligger i skapet ved vinduet.

en.value: The charger that fits this computer is in the cupboard by the window.

spans.value: Clear placement matters more than copying English word for word. First decide which person or thing needs extra information. In these simple patterns, keep the som-clause next to that noun phrase.
A few minutes later, Sara asks Lea whether she has found everything.
Fant du laderen som du trengte?

blocks.translation: Did you find the charger that you needed?

spans.value: Ja, Amir viste meg skapet som står ved vinduet.

blocks.translation: Yes, Amir showed me the cupboard that stands by the window.

spans.value: Bra. Erik er personen som kan hjelpe deg med lampen.

blocks.translation: Good. Erik is the person who can help you with the lamp.

spans.value: Er Erik mannen som Nora snakker med nå?

blocks.translation: Is Erik the man whom Nora is talking to now?

spans.value: Ja, det er han.
Lea now uses both patterns. The cupboard performs the action in som står ved vinduet. Nora performs the action in som Nora snakker med.
Imagine that you are meeting a friend at a busy railway station. Several people are waiting, and several bags stand near the entrance. You need to explain whom and what to look for.
Useful models:

no.value: Jeg venter på en venn som kommer fra Trondheim.

en.value: I’m waiting for a friend who is coming from Trondheim.

no.value: Hun har på seg en jakke som er lett å kjenne igjen.

en.value: She is wearing a jacket that is easy to recognize.

no.value: Kofferten som hun har med seg, er blå.

en.value: The suitcase that she has with her is blue.

no.value: Mannen som står ved billettautomaten, er broren hennes.

en.value: The man who is standing by the ticket machine is her brother.

no.value: Toget som vi skal ta, går om tjue minutter.

en.value: The train that we are going to take leaves in twenty minutes.

spans.value: Without returning to the explanations, the learner should briefly reconstruct the two core patterns, then use each pattern in a new sentence about a person or thing in a familiar place. One sentence should describe someone or something that performs an action; the other should describe someone or something that another person acts on.

prompt.value: Which option correctly identifies the person or thing described by each som-clause in this workshop dialogue? 1. «Hvem er mannen som snakker med Nora?» 2. «Det er han som har nøkkelen til verktøyrommet.» 3. «Jeg trenger en lader som passer til denne PC-en.» 4. «Det ligger en lader i skapet som står ved vinduet.» 5. «Er det skapet som ikke kan låses?» 6. «kvinnen som du møtte ved inngangen» 7. «en lampe som jeg vil reparere»

options.text: 1: Nora («snakker med Nora»); 2: nøkkelen («har nøkkelen til verktøyrommet»); 3: denne PC-en («passer til denne PC-en»); 4: en lader («står ved vinduet»); 5: skapet («ikke kan låses»); 6: du («du møtte ved inngangen»); 7: jeg («jeg vil reparere») — 1: Nora; 2: the key; 3: this computer; 4: a charger; 5: the cupboard; 6: you; 7: I.
options.why: This assigns several clauses to a person or thing inside the clause instead of to the noun phrase being described.

options.text: 1: mannen («snakker med Nora»); 2: han («har nøkkelen til verktøyrommet»); 3: en lader («passer til denne PC-en»); 4: skapet («står ved vinduet»); 5: skapet («ikke kan låses»); 6: kvinnen («du møtte ved inngangen»); 7: en lampe («jeg vil reparere») — 1: the man; 2: him; 3: a charger; 4: the cupboard; 5: the cupboard; 6: the woman; 7: a lamp.
options.why: Each listed noun phrase is the person or thing that the following som-clause identifies.

prompt.value: Combine these notes into one Norwegian sentence: «Vi bruker et program.» «Programmet fungerer på gamle PC-er.» Use noun + som + verb and do not add another subject pronoun after som.

explanation.value: Som introduces the relative clause and represents the described noun; any required preposition remains with its verb inside the clause.

prompt.value: Select the one token that is wrong/needs changing.

payload.feedback: Remove the unnecessary subject pronoun; som already represents the person performing the action.

prompt.value: Which option correctly interprets who performs the action in these paired relative clauses? A. «Jeg kjenner mannen som reparerer lampen.» B. «Jeg kjenner mannen som Lea møtte.»

options.text: A: Mannen reparerer lampen. B: Lea møtte mannen. — A: The man repairs the lamp. B: Lea met the man.
options.why: In A, the noun before som performs the action. In B, Lea is the subject after som and the man receives the action.

options.text: A: Lea reparerer lampen. B: Mannen møtte Lea. — A: Lea repairs the lamp. B: The man met Lea.
options.why: This changes the actor in both clauses instead of following the words after som.

prompt.value: Combine these notes into one Norwegian sentence: «Dette er boka.» «Amir anbefalte boka.» Keep Amir after som and do not repeat boka with an object pronoun.

explanation.value: When the shared noun is the object inside the relative clause, som may be omitted; the subject inside the clause remains overt.

prompt.value: Select the one token that is wrong/needs changing.

payload.feedback: Remove the repeated object pronoun; jakken already fills that role in the som-clause.

prompt.value: Build one Norwegian sentence in which «passer til denne PC-en» clearly describes laderen, not skapet.

explanation.value: Place the relative clause directly after laderen so the description cannot attach to skapet.

prompt.value: Complete the workshop exchange by building one Norwegian sentence. Identify Erik as the person who can help you with the lamp, and identify the lamp that you want to repair.

Write two connected Norwegian sentences for a newly arrived volunteer. Identify Erik as the person who can help with the lamp, and identify a lamp that you want to repair. Use a complete som-clause in each sentence. Do not repeat the described noun or an unnecessary pronoun inside its som-clause.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion.

criteria.instruction: Identifies Erik and the lamp with complete som-clauses in two connected Norwegian sentences.
Does not repeat either described noun or an unnecessary pronoun inside its som-clause.

prompt.value: At a busy railway station, write three short Norwegian sentences for a friend. Identify (1) the man who is standing by the ticket machine, (2) the jacket that is easy to recognize, and (3) the suitcase that Nora has with her. Make the first two described nouns perform the action in their som-clauses, and make Nora perform the action in the third clause. Keep every som-clause next to the noun phrase it describes. Use original wording.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion.

criteria.instruction: Identifies all three specified station people or things with clear som-clauses.
Uses noun + som + verb for the first two descriptions and noun + som + subject + verb for the third description.
Keeps each som-clause next to the noun phrase it describes.

prompt.value: Choose a familiar place other than a workshop or railway station. First write both core som patterns: noun + som + verb, and noun + som + subject + verb. Then write two complete Norwegian sentences about people or things in that place: one where the described noun performs the action, and one where another person acts on the described noun. Use som to add clear identifying information. Do not repeat the described noun or an unnecessary pronoun inside either som-clause.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the task and report evidence for each criterion.

criteria.instruction: Reconstructs both core structures with som: noun + som + verb, and noun + som + subject + verb.
Provides a fresh Norwegian sentence where the described person or thing performs the action after som.
Provides a fresh Norwegian sentence where another person acts on the described person or thing, with that subject retained after som.
Avoids unnecessary repeated nouns or pronouns inside both relative clauses.
